experiment: Oracle Source Test A — Known Source, Hidden Cut

comparison_conventions.error_sign: oracle native frame minus human native frame; negative means earlier
comparison_conventions.GT005_GT008_basis: full fixed slot including human incoming-motion preroll
comparison_conventions.span_iou: inclusive convex source-frame envelope IoU; this intentionally does not reward internal nonlinear piece accuracy
comparison_conventions.visual_similarity: nine evenly sampled output-aligned luma correlations per slot at 270x480; static compositions can produce false confidence

per_shot.mapping_detail: Both monotonic/same-take, but oracle is 1.0x and human samples about 1.201493 native frames per final frame.
per_shot.speed_hold_jump_difference: oracle 1.0x/no hold/no jump; human ~1.20x/no hold/no jump
per_shot.action_phase_difference: Oracle used an early front-to-back rotation including preparation; human used the late action/reveal through result/early hold and omitted preparation.
per_shot.assessment: wrong in/out region inside the correct take

per_shot.mapping_detail: Both monotonic/same-take; oracle is 1.0x while human is about 1.198502x over the content mapping.
per_shot.action_phase_difference: Both preserve cable gather/removal, cleared result and hold; oracle contextual preparation is longer/later than the human transition design.
per_shot.transition_preroll_difference: Human uses 20 final frames from native 709-732. Oracle starts at 752 and labels 63 later contextual frames as preroll: +43-frame length error and no overlap with the actual preroll interval.
per_shot.assessment: good source envelope, wrong phase timing/speed and missed incoming preroll

per_shot.action_phase_difference: Coarse prepare/action/result/hold coverage matches; oracle exits 11 native frames early.
per_shot.assessment: closest shot; cut region is substantially correct, with a small out-point and speed miss

per_shot.action_phase_difference: Both cover late watch action/result/hold, but oracle enters 92 frames late and remains 60 frames too long, shifting the proof beat.
per_shot.assessment: right action family, wrong internal timing and breathing

per_shot.mapping_detail: Both monotonic/same-take; oracle 1.0x versus human ~1.201754x over the content mapping.
per_shot.action_phase_difference: Late lift/reveal, result and hold are retained; oracle starts after most of the human incoming-motion preroll and runs slightly past the human out.
per_shot.transition_preroll_difference: Human preroll is 42 final frames / native 228-277. Oracle contextual preroll is 33 frames beginning at 267: 9 frames too short and 39 native frames late.
per_shot.assessment: moderately close envelope, but transition entry and speed are wrong

per_shot.mapping_detail: Both choose nonlinear compression in one take, but oracle uses 3 forward segments with no holds; human uses 5 pieces with two hold anchors, one forward section, one jump-forward section and a terminal result-hold range.
per_shot.speed_hold_jump_difference: oracle: 3 segments, 0 repeated selections; human: 5 segments, 101 repeated selections and 3 jumps over 2 frames
per_shot.action_phase_difference: Oracle correctly recognizes setup/action compression but ends before the human terminal result/hold at 2064-2075; it overplays intermediate process and misses the intended final landing state.
per_shot.visual_similarity_caution: High correlation is a static-composition false positive; mapping and terminal action state are materially wrong.
per_shot.assessment: correct nonlinear idea, incorrect hold/jump design and terminal result

per_shot.mapping_detail: Oracle plays 76 distinct frames at 1.0x. Human expands only 11 natural source frames across 76 final frames with 65 repeated selections; this is natural low-motion hold selection, not a generated freeze.
per_shot.speed_hold_jump_difference: oracle 1.0x/no repeated selections; human effective ~0.133 source frames per final frame with 65 repeats/no jump
per_shot.action_phase_difference: Both choose result/hold rather than the full placement action, so phase choice is right; the exact result micro-range and breathing treatment are wrong.
per_shot.visual_similarity_caution: High correlation reflects near-static result composition and does not mean the hold mapping matches.
per_shot.assessment: right phase, wrong micro-range and hold/speed mapping

per_shot.mapping_detail: Both are continuous monotonic CTA gestures at the family level, but oracle picked an earlier repeated CTA take; human uses AU0122_03 and ~1.197719x mapping.
per_shot.action_phase_difference: Both contain hero reset/point/result breathing, but they are different physical takes; the gesture timing and pose are not the human choice.
per_shot.assessment: correct source but wrong repeated take and wrong cut region

aggregate.mapping_family_recognition: 7/8 broadly correct; GT009 nonlinear family recognized but piece design wrong; GT010 hold mapping missed
aggregate.systematic_speed_error: For six ordinary monotonic shots, human mapping is about 1.196-1.207 native frames/final frame while oracle used 1.0x.
aggregate.largest_error_class: source in/out and internal take-region selection
aggregate.secondary_error_class: speed/hold/jump mapping, especially GT009 and GT010
aggregate.transition_result: TR001 actual 20-frame preroll was missed; TR002 was entered 39 native frames late and made 9 frames too short

verdict.A_known_source_can_ai_edit_like_human: NO — not reliably. GT006 is close; GT005 and GT008 have useful overlap; five shots remain materially wrong in cut region, take choice or mapping.
verdict.B_primary_error: Internal source-region selection (in/out and repeated-take choice), followed by systematic 1.0x-vs-~1.2x speed error and missing nonlinear/hold treatment.
verdict.C_next_step: Do not move the main effort to Source Matcher yet. Correct-source input did not isolate the problem away; first improve cut-point/action-state selection and same-take compression/hold decisions.
